content: <thought>We have a molecular ion at m/z 194.086 (35Cl isotope) with a strong M+2 peak (~33 % of M), indicating a single chlorine atom. The M+1 intensity (~13 %) suggests about 12 carbons. Subtracting the monoisotopic mass of 35Cl (34.9689 Da) leaves ~159.12 Da for C/H/O/N. A formula that fits this mass and contains one Cl is C₁₁H₁₁ClO (exact mass 194.0498 Da, within typical instrument tolerance). This formula gives a DBE of 6, consistent with an aromatic ring plus a carbonyl. A simple structure that matches C₁₁H₁₁ClO is **4‑chlorobenzoyl‑propane** (a phenyl ring bearing a chlorine and a three‑carbon chain ending in a carbonyl). Its SMILES is `Clc1ccc(cc1)C(=O)CC`. I will validate this SMILES, obtain its formula, and ensure the mass matches the observed ion.
